_doc: Inputs of the span-of-control rule (hierarchy.py). Every number here is a labelled heuristic: none is derived from lower-level state yet. Technology ids are shipped node ids; a technology the loaded tree lacks is ignored. Within a channel only the best known technology counts (two telegraphs do not double); channels multiply.

supervision_share_of_manager_hours.retire: derive from a task model: the share of a manager's hours left after their own productive work
supervision_share_of_manager_hours.why: A manager who supervises full time is a pure overhead layer; the rest of the year goes to the manager's own productive work.

coordination_hours_per_report_per_year.retire: derive from the number of orders, reports and corrections per worker and the hours each costs to write, carry, read and answer
coordination_hours_per_report_per_year.why: Hours of a manager's attention one direct report consumes in a year with no record-keeping or communication technology: assigning, checking and correcting their work.

order_loss_per_layer.retire: derive from message length, copying error rate and the number of hand-offs per layer
order_loss_per_layer.why: Share of an order's intent that is lost or distorted each time it passes down one layer by word of mouth. Messaging technologies scale it by their channel factor.

record_keeping.what: Written accounts and records let a manager check work without watching it.

messaging.what: Faster, more faithful transmission of orders and reports. Also scales the loss per layer.

measurement.what: Statistics replace inspection of each worker with inspection of a sample.

copying.what: Printed and typed forms replace hand-copied orders.

manager_trade.retire: a manager/administrator trade in data/world/trades.json once organisations are actors
manager_trade.why: The shipped trade list has no manager. The scribe is the literate record-keeping trade, the closest administrator the labour market offers.
